label: weak copy-phase preference for outputting o/m/x; otherwise diffuse
explanation: Sparse (~1% of steps) and diffuse. About 64% of activation mass is in the copy phase, where the clearest signal is the token being output: o (14x lift), m (10x), x (6x), then e and k. Predicting on out_tok in {o,m,x} gets only about half the activations and mass at about 10% precision. Rate peaks at recall_idx 2-4 and in short sequences (L<=5), but adding those conditions trades away recall and F1 stays at or below 0.22. About 29% of the mass is in the original phase, mostly at t=1-3, and is not explained by the input token or the first token. It never fires at t=0 and is weak late in the original phase (orig_idx>=4). Magnitude was not characterized beyond the strongest activations (copy steps that output o/e/x, e.g. input t -> output o).
